question.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
5\sqrt[4]{4x+17}-15=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\sqrt[4]{4x+17}-15 & =0 \\ 5\sqrt[4]{4x+17} & =15 \\ \sqrt[4]{4x+17} & =3 \\ (\sqrt[4]{4x+17})^{4} & ={3}^{4} \\ 4x+17 & =81 \\ 4x & =64 \\ x & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\sqrt[4]{4\cdot 16+17}-15 & =0 \\ 5\sqrt[4]{81}-15 & =0 \\ 5\cdot 3-15 & =0 \\ 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=16.$
